text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Court might close Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islam-based Welfare Party if anti-secularist statements he allegedly made in interview with an Egyptian journalist turn out to be true.
- President Suleyman Demirel says in speeches to military academies that Turkey will always follow the secularist path of founder Kemal Ataturk.
- Trade and Indusry Minister Yalim Erez, who has called for an end to the coalition, says he cannot be silenced by party leader Tansu Ciller.
- Former interior minister Mehmet Agar testifies to commission investigating secularist journalist Ugur Mumcu's murder.
- Turkey estimated to host 10 million holidaymakers in 1997 and raise tourism revenue of $7 billion.
- Turkish army to give series of briefings to journalists, professional organisations and trade unions later this month.
- International Monetary Fund, World Bank, European Union and economists warn Turkey not to put too much importance on high growth rates before implementing sweeping economic reforms.
- Agar says he won't stand as a canditate to replace far-rightist Alparslan Turkes as head of the Nationalist Action Party.
